- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 10% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; increase forecast slope toward true mean by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce volatility.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) for 5+ days, model tends to drift downward; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature decline.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 7–10 days after a spike, model fails to recognize; adjust forecast to align with 3–5-day moving average of true values.
